teams.heading: Fijian rugby player Saimoni Vunilagi dies in Japan of suspected heatstroke
teams.body: The rugby community is mourning the loss of Saimoni Vunilagi after the 26-year-old Fijian back-row forward passed away in Japan. Vunilagi, who played for second-division side Kyushu KV, was hospitalised in Fukuoka on Monday 3 August after displaying severe symptoms of heatstroke following a team practice. Despite medical efforts, he died on Friday 7 August. Kyushu KV released a statement expressing that players and staff are "devastated by this sudden news" as temperatures in Fukuoka reached 35 degrees Celsius.

lead.why: It covers the tragic and high-salience death of Fijian rugby player Saimoni Vunilagi in Japan.

teams.heading: Ollie Lawrence and Elliot Daly lose England central contracts in squad reshuffle
teams.body: Steve Borthwick has dropped centre Ollie Lawrence and versatile back Elliot Daly from England's 25-man central contract list. The omission comes as Borthwick reshapes his squad ahead of next year's World Cup in Australia, making five changes to the group who receive around £150,000 a season. While Borthwick handed contracts to Northampton forward Alex Coles and Sale prop Asher Opoku-Fordjour, Lawrence and Daly must now fight back from the margins.

teams.heading: Ireland mourns as legendary Irish Times writer Edmund Van Esbeck dies
teams.body: The Irish rugby community is mourning legendary journalist Edmund 'Ned' Van Esbeck, who has died aged 94. Van Esbeck spent more than 30 years covering the sport for The Irish Times, writing his weekly column from 1968 until 2002. He chronicled 18 overseas tours with Ireland and the Lions, and wrote several authoritative books, including Irish Rugby 1874-1999. IRFU CEO Kevin Potts paid tribute to Van Esbeck, who was a respected voice during the sport's amateur and professional eras.

lead.why: The passing of legendary Irish Times rugby correspondent Edmund Van Esbeck is the day's highest-salience news story.

teams.heading: Scottish rugby remains on alert as landmark concussion lawsuit proceeds in court
teams.body: The wider game, including Scottish rugby's governing body, is monitoring developments closely after a UK court delivered a landmark decision allowing the rugby concussion lawsuits to proceed. The group litigation had previously faced a critical period of uncertainty, with reports last week suggesting the legal action was at risk of being dismissed following a change of legal representation by the claimants. With the court now allowing the case to move forward, the governing bodies face a prolonged legal battle over player brain injuries.

teams.heading: Wales legend Alun Wyn Jones joins Ospreys board during survival fight
teams.body: Former Wales captain Alun Wyn Jones has joined the Ospreys board of directors with immediate effect. The 40-year-old former lock, who won 158 caps for Wales, returns at a turbulent time for his former club. Under Welsh Rugby Union plans to cut professional men's teams to three, either the Swansea-based Ospreys or the Scarlets will be axed by 2028. Jones wants to bring his experience 'to help drive long-term growth and stability for the organisation.'

lead.why: The return of Wales legend Alun Wyn Jones to the Ospreys board during a critical battle for regional survival is the day's biggest story.

teams.heading: Les Kiss names bolstered Wallabies squad for two Tests in Argentina
teams.body: Australia head coach Les Kiss has handed Los Pumas a warning by naming fit-again midfielders Len Ikitau and Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii in a 34-man touring squad. The Wallabies, who recently registered back-to-back victories over Japan, will travel to Argentina for two Tests, starting in San Salvador de Jujuy before heading to Mendoza. While the visitors welcome back their star backline duo, they will be without injured prop Zane Nonggorr and the suspended Miles Amatosero.

teams.body: The Japanese rugby community is in mourning following the death of 26-year-old Fijian player Saimoni Vunilagi. Vunilagi passed away after suffering suspected heatstroke during a training session in Japan. The incident underscores the extreme environmental challenges facing athletes during the current summer heat. While the Brave Blossoms remain 10th in the standings, this tragedy has overshadowed tactical reviews following their recent loss to France. Player welfare and safety protocols have now become the primary focus for both domestic clubs and the international setup.

teams.heading: Dave Rennie names Fabian Holland to start against South Africa in Johannesburg
teams.body: Head coach Dave Rennie has made just one change to the starting XV that defeated Ireland, handing fit-again lock Fabian Holland a start for today’s series opener in Johannesburg. Holland replaces Patrick Tuipulotu in the second row, while Josh Moorby retains his place on the wing. Rennie noted there is "massive competition for places" in a squad that sees Damian McKenzie fit to start at full-back. A win today would see New Zealand leapfrog the Springboks to reclaim the world No. 1 ranking.

lead.why: It covers the matchday squad announcement for the opening Test against South Africa, featuring a significant selection in the second row.

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus names Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu as South Africa's starting fly-half
teams.body: Rassie Erasmus described the decision to start Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu and Grant Williams against the All Blacks as "touch-and-go" ahead of Saturday's series opener. The pair are preferred to Manie Libbok and Cobus Reinach for the Ellis Park clash, while Handré Pollard misses the matchday squad entirely. With Siya Kolisi absent for the first Test of the tour, Pieter-Steph du Toit captains the side from the back-row. The fixture also marks a landmark for Damian de Allende, who earns his 100th cap.
